entries.description: Operator set pathAwareCritique: advisory.

Registered S1 via start_session (claude/anthropic/claude-opus-5/high); read the preload, the spec, and the Session Set Configuration block. Confirmed the operator precondition: the published answer key resolved HEAD=2acc7b7 via git ls-remote, matching the local reference solution's master. No placeholder URL is inherited.

Extracted both service contracts as LITERAL wire bodies from a real run rather than by reading source: started converter (:5101) and persistence (:5102) from the reference solution and captured POST /convert 200 + 400 (bad file, unknown schema), GET /schemas, POST /batches 201 + 200-duplicate + 400, and GET /batches/{id}. Recorded in s1-service-contracts.md with the capture recipe.

Settled Part D by PROVING it, with a falsifier. Started a second converter on :5201 alongside :5101 (both healthy at once); repointed the watcher by configuration only (Watcher__Converter__BaseAddress), no code edited or rebuilt; processed a CSV end to end; then KILLED the converter on :5101 and confirmed the pipeline still worked. All four decision-table rows forced live (Stored / AlreadyStored / Rejected / Deferred), including a deferred file retried and stored on a later tick. Port allocation fixed at 51xx=yours, 52xx=the version you test against. Recorded that this proves the repoint MECHANISM, not cross-implementation conformance (same build on both ports).

Settled layout and naming via a two-engine decision consult (gpt-5-4 + gemini-pro, bias-cautions preamble, raw in s1-layout-naming-consensus.json). decision_consensus.enabled is false repo-wide; the consult was run per the spec's instruction without touching the config flag. Both engines converged on owner-in-slug, so the result was synthesized rather than escalated. Ruled: slug {owner}-{service}, title {Service} ({Owner}), code root modules/{owner}/{service}, member-major manifest order, one CODEOWNERS line per member. This REVISES the spec's POC recommendation (converter-v1): version-in-slug stays unique only with central version allocation, contradicting 'nobody waits on anybody'.

Confirmed the POC's four findings against the RUNNING PRODUCT, not just the model functions. Authored src/test/poc-nine-modules-ondisk.ts: writes a real nine-module workspace to disk and drives classifyModulesManifest -> readSessionSets -> computeVisibleModules -> buildVisibleModulePayloads (the payload the shipping renderer receives since Set 092). 5 passing: nine declared rows from the product's own parser and discovery; grouping exactly one level deep with no per-member tier; manifest order beats alphabetical (with a guard that the fixture actually distinguishes them); day-one nine-empty renders warning-free; and the version-slug collision condition pinned as an assertion. Re-ran the original poc-nine-modules.ts: 4 passing.

Routed an analysis (task_type=analysis, excl. anthropic -> gemini-2.5-pro) of the draft outline against the concept-ownership table, adopt-dabbler.md and hello-world.md. Raw in s1-outline-ownership-review.json. One Critical accepted whole (the prerequisite list omitted the reader's entry state - they would stall on instruction one; R8 split into R8a entry state and R8b build installs). One Major accepted as a real hazard but REJECTED as a fix: it asked R4 to link to adopt-dabbler.md Part 5, which Session 3 deletes; R4 now records the transfer plus a hard S2-writes-before-S3-deletes ordering constraint.

Wrote s1-walk-outline.md: rulings R1-R8b, the four parts with independent finish lines, the single happy path, the ownership table, and the handover to Sessions 2/3/4. Also recorded R8b, a factual correction to the spec's prose: the success criterion's 'nothing but the .NET 10 SDK' is false - LocalDB is a separate MSI product (verified against this machine's installed-products registry) and there is no winget package for it alone. Flagged for the operator; the spec assigned this to Session 4, which is too late because Session 2 writes the prerequisite list.

Build and test. Reference solution: dotnet build succeeded (SDK 10.0.201, pinned by global.json). Extension unit suite via the vscode-stub mocha path: 1821 passing. pytest: see the verification conventions block for the recorded baseline.

Registered S2 via start_session (claude/anthropic/claude-opus-5/high). Read the four preload files, the spec (Session Set Configuration block: full tier, requiresUAT true, requiresE2E false, uatStyle ad-hoc, uatScope per-set, pathAwareCritique advisory) and the S2 plan. Decision-review-queue: absent, nothing to triage.

Confirmed S1 Creates exist and are non-empty: s1-service-contracts.md (both contracts as literal captured wire bodies) and s1-walk-outline.md (rulings R1-R9, four parts, ownership table, handover). Read both in full plus s1-conventions.md. S1 closed VERIFIED; answer key published at github.com/darndestdabbler/dabbler-ai-orchestration-multimodule-demo, so there is no placeholder to inherit.

Wrote docs/tutorials/three-module-pipeline.md (1229 lines) against s1-walk-outline.md, holding R1-R9 as settled. Four parts, each with a behavioural finish line and a Coming-back-to-this state block. No declaration step in Parts A/B/C (R9 owns declaration). Answer key linked by its real published URL; no placeholder written.

Part D written as the payoff: two configuration values, no code change, one machine, localhost throughout. Per-member database via the ConnectionStrings__Orders environment override, so a teammate service runs without editing any file in their code root. Solo limitation stated plainly (two copies of one build prove the repoint mechanism, not cross-implementation conformance). Cross-machine variant is appendix-only with the firewall step marked unverified.

Re-established the quotable literals by RUNNING the reference solution today rather than trusting the S1 transcription: dotnet --list-sdks, sqllocaldb info, the full dotnet test summary (31/24/19 = 74) and the Phase A decision-table filter (12 tests, 81 ms). Wrote a checker (scratchpad/check_literals.py) that extracts every wire-body / test-summary line from the tutorial and fails unless it appears verbatim in a provenance source: 14/14 traceable. It caught one fabrication in my own draft - a Stored transcript whose fileName I had changed while keeping the real batchId - which was removed.

Mechanical duplication scan over twelve procedure phrases owned by other documents (Marketplace, Install ai-router, branch protection, git clone, venv/pip, Copilot CLI, Delete Module, approval settings): zero hits. New Module appears once, as a named link-out to adopt-dabbler Part 3, not as an explanation.

Routed two off-provider reviews (anthropic excluded). (1) Duplication / ownership / S3-fragility review vs the pre-trim adopt-dabbler.md, hello-world.md and release-and-recovery.md -> s2-duplication-review.json: one Major S3-fragility (the touches: passage cited the app/greeter example that lives in adopt-dabbler Part 5, which S3 deletes - the reference would dangle), two Minor broken handoffs (Parts 1-2 should be Part 1; Part 3 should be Parts 2-3), one Minor duplication. All four acted on. (2) Documentation review against ten named rules incl. host-neutrality -> s2-documentation-review.json: 9/10 pass, one Major on the mkdir commands.

DISMISSED the documentation review Major as stated, on evidence: it claimed creating a folder at the root of C: needs administrator rights and that mkdir is not recursive. Probed both on this machine in a non-elevated PowerShell - mkdir C:\<new>\incomingrchive succeeded and created the intermediate folder, so both stated mechanisms are false, and its proposed fix would have put an unexpandable ~/Documents path into appsettings.json. Kept the residual (a locked-down managed workstation could still refuse) and fixed it by REMOVAL per the simplicity-first convention: three mkdir lines collapsed to two, plus one sentence saying any writable folder works.

Ran verify_session --phase discovery (fan-out 2, all severities) with s2-conventions.md as the up-front conventions block. Round 1 returned ISSUES FOUND: six Majors, five nits. The raw artifact s2-verification.md was written, but a 10-minute harness timeout killed the process before it could write s2-issues.json or patch disposition.json - so the paid verifier output survived (artifact-first write order, L-079-1) while the findings envelope did not. Both --phase supplementary and --phase remediation-review refuse to run without that envelope, so the loop could not advance on round 1.

Did NOT hand-author the missing envelope - writing a verification artifact by hand is mixed-mode drift and is forbidden. Took the sanctioned alternative instead: accepted all six Majors (none disputed), fixed them once, fixed four of five nits, answered the fifth, wrote s2-remediation-round-1.md, and re-ran --phase discovery on the corrected document. Within the 2-discovery-pass bound; regenerates the envelope through the blessed writer; and a full re-read is stronger than the fix-delta review it replaces, since a delta reviewer cannot see what already sits in its baseline (the failure that let two of S1 twelve Majors escape six rounds). Deviation recorded, not performed quietly.

Proved verification Major 4 rather than accepting it on argument: probed Windows PowerShell 5.1 native-stdout redirection on this machine and got first bytes ff fe - a UTF-16LE BOM. curl output redirected with > would reach persistence as UTF-16 and be rejected as malformed JSON, sending the reader to debug their own correct code. Switched to curl -o. Same evidence-first treatment as the earlier mkdir finding, which went the other way and was dismissed.

Discovery round 2 (fan-out 2/2, gpt-5-6) on the corrected document: four Majors and five nits in the merged envelope. Majors 1 and 3 are the same defect found independently by both arms - and it was introduced by round 1 own remediation: the fix for the hard-coded batch id put the capture in step 5, which meant step 5 called /run-now a second time after step 4 had already archived the only file. Found during a coherence read while round 2 was still running and fixed before the round returned; round 2 reviewed the pre-fix text. Third time in this set that remediation introduced a fresh defect (S1 recorded four).

All four Majors accepted, none disputed; all five nits fixed. Major 2 (ports never required by the build instructions, so a correct converter would fail every probe on 5101) fixed twice over: Listening on 5101/5102 added to the What to build lists, and --urls added to all five main-path dotnet run commands. Major 4 (reusing orders.csv collides in archive and returns AlreadyStored) fixed with a concrete Copy-Item to a unique name plus both consequences named. Nits: readback commands added to Parts B and C finish lines, the ScheduleEnabled poll race documented with its recovery, the cross-machine appendix corrected to bind BOTH services and carry the per-member database, and the too-categorical timeout-means-firewall claim rewritten. Wrote s2-remediation-round-2.md.

No build or code test applies: the session diff contains zero .py and zero .ts files - one new markdown tutorial plus session bookkeeping and raw routed artifacts. The relevant suite is the answer key it quotes, re-run today from D:/Projects/dabbler-csv-pipeline: 74 passing (31/24/19), 0 failed, 0 skipped. guidance_report --check OK at 10,895/12,000 tokens (91%). The repo pytest suite was started and had produced no output after 60+ minutes, so it was stopped; this session adds no Python to the package, so its count is inherited per the S1 precedent and cannot have been moved by this work.

Ran verify_session --phase remediation-review on the fix delta: VERIFIED, 0 findings, 3 fix verdicts accepted / 0 rejected (L3 recorded as duplicate-of L1). The reviewer additionally checked the new PowerShell flows, Part D outcome handling and cross-machine bindings for remediation-introduced blocking defects and found none. Loop closed inside the bounds: 2 discovery passes and 1 remediation-review cycle, no operator authorisation needed.
Authored disposition.json for S2 (preserving the patched verification fields), committed and pushed, ran close_session, then fired the session-complete notification.
